description: bash init.sh brings the demo-mode dev server up from cold on the project's own port (build/ports.json) and --stop tears it down.
verification: bash init.sh >/dev/null && curl -fsS -o /dev/null http://localhost:$(jq -r .dev build/ports.json)/ && bash init.sh --stop >/dev/null

description: Executable layer rules: domain stays pure, fetch() only in the API client, UI depends on ports not adapters, no AWS SDK or VITE_ secrets in the browser bundle, backend reuses the rules engine.
The PreToolUse guard blocks merges, protected-branch pushes, force pushes, gate bypasses, deploys (incl. sam/aws) and shell-wrapper evasions while allowing benign look-alikes.
quality-sweep.sh exits zero: architecture, config integrity, registry re-verification, debug artifacts, doc validity, secrets, guardrails, dead exports.
Layer 3: main requires review, required check 'build-and-test', and admins cannot bypass (run harden-github.sh after the first push).
verification: gh api repos/$(git remote get-url origin | sed -E 's#.*github\.com[:/]([^/]+/[^/.]+)(\.git)?#\1#')/branches/main/protection | jq -e '.enforce_admins.enabled == true and .required_pull_request_reviews.required_approving_review_count >= 1'

knip reports no unused files, exports or dependencies (tailwindcss is CSS-imported and allowlisted).

description: A pick cannot change once the week's shared deadline passes, but can change right up to it.
The app runs on real time by default so countdowns and lock states match reality; the commissioner can still pin the clock, and tests pin it for determinism.
verification: grep -q 'let pinned: Date | null = null' src/data/demo/clock.ts && grep -q 'survivor:demo:clock:v1' tests/e2e/helpers.ts

description: All 32 team logos are served from public/team-logos/ (fetched from ESPN's CDN by npm run logos:fetch) instead of two-letter monograms; a missing or broken logo falls back to the team-coloured monogram.
verification: test "$(ls public/team-logos/*.png | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" -eq 32 && grep -q 'team-logos/' src/components/TeamMonogram.tsx && grep -q 'setFailed(true)' src/components/TeamMonogram.tsx

description: Kickoffs and deadlines render in the league's own timezone (displayTimeZone, America/Chicago) with the zone abbreviation, so every member quotes the same clock. Timestamps stay UTC in storage.
verification: jq -e '.league.settings.displayTimeZone == "America/Chicago"' src/data/demo/fixtures/demo-season.json >/dev/null && ! grep -rn 'formatKickoff([^,)]*)' src/features --include='*.tsx' | grep -v timeZone

description: The whole league locks at ONE deadline, a configurable lead before the week's first kickoff (default 5 minutes). A Monday-night pick is as locked as a Sunday-morning one, missing picks are struck from that moment, and every pick becomes public then. Enforced in the domain and again on the API with the server clock.
A team on bye cannot be selected.
verification: npx vitest run src/domain/rules/picks.test.ts -t 'rejects a team on bye'

description: No pick is pending while the week is open and a miss once the last game kicks off; weeks without schedule data never strike anyone.
Re-applying the same result observation is a no-op; corrections bump the version once; commissioner results lock against provider overwrites.
A commissioner result override recalculates lives, eliminations and champions from scratch.
Everyone out in the same week yields co-champions by default or tied finalists pending a recorded commissioner decision.
verification: npx vitest run src/domain/rules/engine.test.ts -t 'eliminated in the same week'

description: Cancelled games void the pick (or count as a miss per settings) and return the team; postponed games stay pending.
Other players' picks are hidden until kickoff; own picks and the commissioner's view are never redacted (domain + API).
The API re-validates deadlines (server clock), team reuse, eliminations and roles on every pick; writes are version-conditional (409 on races).

The Lambda results sync uses the SAME domain ESPN parser as the browser (skipping unknown teams rather than guessing); commissioners can enter schedules/results manually when the provider is down (503 surfaced).

The app ships the REAL NFL schedule (272 games, 18 weeks) cached from ESPN, not invented matchups: every week is provider-sourced and every seeded pick resolves to a real game. Refresh it with npm run schedule:fetch.
verification: jq -e '(.season.isSynthetic == false) and ([.weeks[] | select(.source != "provider")] | length == 0) and ((.games | length) == 272)' src/data/demo/fixtures/demo-season.json >/dev/null && node -e 'const s=require("./src/data/demo/fixtures/demo-season.json");const ids=new Set(s.games.map(g=>g.id));const bad=s.picks.filter(p=>!ids.has(p.gameId));if(bad.length){console.error("picks not linked to a real game:",bad.map(p=>p.playerId));process.exit(1)}'

description: Live schedule and scores come from ESPN's public scoreboard for the correct week. The parser is shared by the browser and the Lambda; the first sync replaces the placeholder slate and re-links picks to the real fixtures by team; re-syncing is idempotent and never overwrites a commissioner result. NOTE: the live browser call cannot be exercised in CI (no outbound network), so the request shape and failure paths are covered with a stubbed fetch and the parser against a real captured payload.
verification: npx vitest run src/domain/nfl src/data/nfl src/data/demo/sync.test.ts --reporter=dot

description: Both Lambda handlers bundle with esbuild (AWS SDK external).
verification: node backend/build.mjs && test -f backend/dist/api/index.mjs && test -f backend/dist/syncResults/index.mjs

description: A valid JPG/PNG/WebP under 5 MB gets presigned POSTs and finalizes after the API verifies both objects.
Unsupported types (gif, svg) and oversized/empty images are rejected before a ticket is issued and again at finalize (object deleted).
Replacing a headshot deletes the previous objects; removing restores the default avatar.
Players without a headshot, or whose image fails to load, show the default avatar with meaningful alt text.
The Vite base is derived from VITE_BASE_PATH or GITHUB_REPOSITORY and never assumed to be '/'; user/org sites resolve to '/'.
npm run build emits a static site (index.html, base-aware 404.html, .nojekyll, hashed assets) deployable directly to GitHub Pages.
verification: npx vite build --base=/Survivor/ --outDir dist-e2e >/dev/null && test -f dist-e2e/index.html && grep -q "var base = '/Survivor/'" dist-e2e/404.html && test -f dist-e2e/.nojekyll && grep -q '/Survivor/assets/' dist-e2e/index.html

description: scripts/serve-static.mjs behaves like GitHub Pages (base-only serving, 301 on bare repo path, real 404 with 404.html, no SPA rewrite).
Under /Survivor/: boots with zero 404s, nested-route refresh keeps the page, clean deep links are rewritten by 404.html, unknown routes render Not Found.

The published GitHub Pages build offers no way to pick: no sign-in, no Pick or Me nav, no make/change-pick calls to action, and write routes redirect to the league. In demo mode a visitor's pick could never reach anyone else, so offering the controls would mislead people into believing they had entered. Running locally (the commissioner's machine) and connected mode stay fully interactive.
verification: npx vitest run src/config/env.test.ts --reporter=dot && npx playwright test --project=published

description: Demo mode runs entirely from static files: league home, sign-in, make/change pick, locked picks, grid, my-season, mobile navigation.
Commissioner adds players, corrects results (standings recalculate), imports CSV with a blocking report, sets picks after kickoff, moves the demo clock; non-commissioners are redirected.
axe-core reports no WCAG 2.x A/AA violations on the ten primary screens, desktop and mobile.
The seeded season regenerates byte-identically from the committed schedule cache, so fixture generation never depends on the network.
verification: cp src/data/demo/fixtures/demo-season.json node_modules/.tmp/fixture.before.json && npm run -s fixtures:generate >/dev/null && cmp -s node_modules/.tmp/fixture.before.json src/data/demo/fixtures/demo-season.json

description: Every player has a real headshot, imported from the commissioner's photos by npm run headshots:import (EXIF-aware, face-aware square crop, 128px + 512px WebP). A player without a photo falls back to the neutral default avatar — no generated stand-in ever poses as someone's face.
verification: test -f public/headshots/default.svg && test -f public/headshots/manifest.json && jq -e '[.images[] | select(.contentType=="image/webp")] | length >= 9' src/data/demo/fixtures/demo-season.json >/dev/null && jq -e '[.profiles[] | select(.imageId == null)] | length == 0' src/data/demo/fixtures/demo-season.json
